articles.title: Oncoclínicas obtém apoio de credores para renegociar dívida de R$ 5,7 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Plano de recuperação extrajudicial já recebeu adesão de credores com mais de R$ 3,5 bilhões a receber, o equivalente a 61,6% das dívidas incluídas no processo; empresa agora pedirá homologação à Justiça.
articles.summary: Plano de recuperação extrajudicial já recebeu adesão de credores com mais de R$ 3,5 bilhões a receber, o equivalente a 61,6% das dívidas incluídas no processo.
articles.body:
A Oncoclínicas atingiu o apoio de credores que representam 61,6% das dívidas incluídas em seu plano de recuperação extrajudicial, superando o mínimo exigido por lei para dar andamento ao processo.

Segundo fato relevante divulgado nesta sexta-feira (30), os credores que aderiram ao plano têm mais de R$ 3,5 bilhões em créditos a receber.

O percentual supera o quórum mínimo de 50% necessário para a aprovação do plano, considerando o valor total das dívidas abrangidas pelo processo, sem incluir débitos entre empresas do próprio grupo.

Essa base de créditos soma aproximadamente R$ 5,7 bilhões.

Com o apoio necessário alcançado, a companhia informou que dará prosseguimento ao pedido de homologação do plano na Justiça. A homologação é a etapa em que o juiz analisa e confirma formalmente o acordo, permitindo que ele produza seus efeitos legais.

O processo de recuperação extrajudicial tramita na 3ª Vara de Falências e Recuperações Judiciais de São Paulo e envolve a Oncoclínicas e algumas de suas subsidiárias, empresas controladas pelo grupo.

A próxima etapa prevê a publicação de um edital, conforme determina a Lei de Recuperação Judicial e Falências. O documento dará publicidade ao processo e permitirá que os credores apresentem eventuais impugnações, ou seja, questionamentos sobre o plano.

A companhia afirmou que o plano atualizado foi apresentado à Justiça na quinta-feira (29) e reiterou as informações divulgadas no fato relevante do dia anterior. O documento está disponível no site da empresa e nos autos do processo judicial.

articles.title: Trump diz que EUA investigam se ataque contra a Binance foi feito por hackers da Coreia do Norte | G1
articles.standfirst: Autores de ataque roubaram US$ 6,3 bilhões da maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo.
articles.summary: Autores de ataque roubaram US$ 6,3 bilhões da maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo.
articles.body:
O presidente americano Donald Trump afirmou nesta sexta-feira (30) que os Estados Unidos estão investigando se hackers da Coreia do Norte estão por trás do ataque hacker contra a Binance, maior corretora de criptomoedas do mundo .

"Estamos investigando", disse Trump a jornalistas na Casa Branca, ao ser questionado se o ataque deveria ser atribuído a um grupo de hackers da Coreia do Norte.

"Você sabe como era antigamente, quando você assinava um cheque e o sacava? Essas pessoas são diferentes. Nunca mais vemos o dinheiro. Então, sempre achei isso um pouco perigoso", afirmou.

A ação contra a Binance levou cerca de 20 minutos, terminou com o roubo de US$ 6,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 34 bilhões) e é apontada como o maior ataque hacker da história do setor de criptomoedas.

Donald Trump, presidente dos Estados Unidos, em foto de 30 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: AFP/Alex Wroblewski

Segundo a Reuters, a Binance está trabalhando com autoridades policiais em todo o mundo, incluindo o Departamento Federal de Investigação (FBI) e o Serviço Secreto dos Estados Unidos (USSS).

As empresas americanas TRM Labs e Chainalysis, especializadas em rastrear movimentações de criptomoedas, afirmam que os responsáveis pelo roubo são hackers ligados à Coreia do Norte.

Mas a Binance afirmou pela manhã que não tinha identificado os criminosos.

A empresa informou que investimentos de clientes brasileiros permanecem seguros porque são ativos mantidos em cold wallets , conhecidas como carteiras frias. Apesar da garantia de segurança, os saques de criptomoedas foram temporariamente suspensos.

🔎 Cold wallet, ou carteira fria, é uma forma de guardar criptomoedas que mantém as chaves necessárias para movimentá-las desconectadas da internet. Isso dificulta a ação de hackers e reduz o risco de roubos virtuais, mas não elimina completamente a possibilidade de perdas.

Em comunicado, a Binance disse que, no Brasil, segue as regras do Banco Central, que, desde fevereiro, exige a separação dos recursos dos usuários aos da corretora. A exigência, porém, não elimina o risco de ataques hackers nem garante o ressarcimento de eventuais perdas.

articles.title: Conta de luz: Aneel mantém bandeira verde em novembro sem taxa | G1
articles.standfirst: Bandeira verde na tarifa de energia elétrica significa que a conta não terá custo extra. A bandeira tarifária sinaliza ao consumidor os custos reais da geração de energia no país.
articles.summary: A Aneel confirmou que a conta de luz continuará com bandeira verde em novembro, garantindo que o consumidor não pague taxas extras pela geração de energia no mês.
articles.body:
A bandeira tarifaria de novembro será verde , anunciou a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica ( Aneel ) nesta sexta-feira (30). Isso significa que não haverá cobrança adicional na conta este mês . ( entenda mais abaixo )

🔎 A bandeira tarifária sinaliza ao consumidor os custos reais da geração de energia no país. Quando a geração fica mais cara, a cobrança extra é aplicada automaticamente nas contas.

De maio a setembro, a bandeira tarifária estava em nível amarelo, o que significava uma cobrança adicional de R$ 1,88 a cada 100kWh consumidos.

"A bandeira verde, que está em vigor desde outubro, permanece em novembro devido às condições favoráveis de geração, com o aumento de chuvas nas regiões onde estão localizadas as principais usinas hidrelétricas, o que traz equilíbrio nos reservatórios. Nesse cenário, não haverá necessidade de maior acionamento de termelétricas, cujo custo é mais elevado", disse a agência.

💡 O sistema de cores da Aneel sinaliza as condições de geração de energia. Se chove pouco e as hidrelétricas geram menos, é preciso acionar usinas termelétricas, que são mais caras.

💡 Para pagar por essas usinas, a Aneel aciona as bandeiras amarela, vermelha 1 ou vermelha 2, com taxas extras na conta de luz.

Bandeira significa cobrança de um adicional às contas de energia — Foto: Divulgação

Cada bandeira tarifária acionada pela Aneel pode gerar um custo extra ao consumidor:

🟩bandeira verde (condições favoráveis de geração de energia) – sem custo extra;

🟨bandeira amarela (condições menos favoráveis) – R$ 18,85 por MWh (megawatt-hora) utilizado (ou R$ 1,88 a cada 100kWh);

🟥bandeira vermelha patamar 1 (condições desfavoráveis) – R$ 44,63 por MWh utilizado (ou R$ 4,46 a cada 100 kWh);

🟥🟥bandeira vermelha patamar 2 (condições muito desfavoráveis) – R$ 78,77 por MWh utilizado (ou R$ 7,87 a cada 100 kWh).

articles.title: Raízen aprova plano para sair de crise de R$ 65 bilhões e será dividida em duas empresas | G1
articles.standfirst: Plano prevê aporte de até R$ 3,5 bilhões da Shell, conversão de dívidas em participação na companhia e separação das operações de combustíveis e de açúcar e etanol em duas empresas independentes.
articles.summary: Plano de recuperação extrajudicial foi aprovado pelos acionistas nesta sexta-feira e prevê aumento de capital entre R$ 3,5 bilhões e R$ 39,8 bilhões.
articles.body:
Os acionistas da Raízen aprovaram nesta sexta-feira (30) medidas necessárias para colocar em prática o plano de recuperação extrajudicial (RE) da companhia.

Com dívida de cerca de R$ 65 bilhões, é a maior RE da história do Brasil. A crise da companhia ocorreu após uma série de apostas arriscadas, safras ruins e preços baixos das commodities .

Entre as decisões estão mudanças nos estatutos das empresas , alterações no capital social , a separação dos negócios de energia e combustíveis e a eleição dos novos conselhos de administração .

O plano prevê um aumento de capital de até R$ 39,8 bilhões .

Desse total, a Shell poderá aportar até R$ 3,5 bilhões , enquanto a Aguassanta poderá contribuir com até R$ 500 milhões , caso decida participar.

A operação também prevê a conversão de parte das dívidas de credores em participação na empresa e a possibilidade de os demais acionistas comprarem novas ações para manter sua participação na companhia.

O aumento de capital ainda será submetido à aprovação do Conselho de Administração, em reunião prevista para 6 de novembro.

Os acionistas terão de 9 de novembro a 8 de dezembro para exercer o direito de preferência , ou seja, a prioridade para comprar novas ações antes que elas sejam oferecidas a outros investidores.

Outra mudança aprovada prevê a divisão da Raízen em duas companhias abertas , independentes e com ações negociadas na bolsa.

A Raízen Energia ficará responsável pela produção e comercialização de etanol, açúcar e bioenergia. Já a Raízen S.A. concentrará as atividades de distribuição de combustíveis e lubrificantes da marca Shell.

A separação será realizada após o cumprimento das condições previstas no plano e dos prazos legais. Para viabilizar a operação, os acionistas também aprovaram a redução do capital social da Raízen S.A. em até R$ 35 bilhões, por meio da entrega aos acionistas de títulos emitidos pela Raízen Energia.

As assembleias também aprovaram a formação dos novos conselhos de administração das empresas. Após a conclusão do aumento de capital, cada conselho terá sete membros titulares e sete suplentes.

Para presidir o conselho da empresa de distribuição de combustíveis e lubrificantes, foi indicado Samuel Aguirre . Na empresa de etanol, açúcar e bioenergia, a indicação é Julio Cesar de Toledo Piza Neto .

A liderança dos negócios de distribuição de combustíveis ficará a cargo de Lorival Nogueira Luz Jr ., enquanto Geovane Dilkin Consul foi indicado para comandar a operação de etanol, açúcar e bioenergia.

Ambos fazem parte da atual administração da companhia e participam do processo de transformação operacional e financeira em andamento há dois anos. As indicações ainda deverão ser confirmadas pelos respectivos conselhos.

A companhia também informou que começará a preparar um processo para avaliar a possibilidade de receber investimentos no negócio de distribuição de combustíveis.

Uma das alternativas previstas é a oferta pública secundária, operação em que acionistas vendem ações que já possuem a outros investidores.

Segundo o CEO da Raízen S.A., Nelson Gomes , as decisões aprovadas dão previsibilidade à reorganização e permitem dar continuidade ao plano de transformação da companhia.

"O trabalho realizado até aqui é fruto da construção conjunta entre todas as partes interessadas, e também da disciplina no cumprimento de todos os compromissos assumidos ao longo do processo de reestruturação da companhia", afirmou.

A administração atual das empresas permanecerá inalterada até que sejam cumpridas as condições necessárias para a conclusão das mudanças.

articles.title: Exxon and Chevron report massive profits after Trump brags U.S. energy companies are ‘making a freaking fortune’ just before midterms
articles.summary: Wars and geopolitical risks prove profitable, although Big Oil eyes more long-term certainty.
articles.body:
ExxonMobil and Chevron reported profits Friday from almost $10 billion to over $15 billion amid the Iran war that's triggering high oil prices and skyrocketing refining margins. Big Oil's big earnings come amid President Donald Trump touting the "freaking fortune" U.S. oil companies are raking in during rallies ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

The war has pushed oil prices well above $100 per barrel and U.S. gasoline costs to autumn records and diesel to all-time highs. Driven by spiking refining profits, Exxon posted a third-quarter profit of $15.4 billion, more than double the $7.5 billion profit from the same quarter a year ago, and just shy of its highest quarterly profit ever in 2022. Likewise, Chevron's earnings of $9.9 billion were well up from $3.5 billion a year ago.

"We recognize the impact high prices have on people's lives and economic growth," said Exxon CEO Darren Woods during Friday's earnings call. "We always have, which is why we have been constantly focused on efficiently growing advantaged production to keep markets supplied. That focus and commitment pays off in times like this."

He specifically cited a large refining expansion in Beaumont, Texas, in 2023 that he said has kept prices from rising even higher.

The earnings reports—including huge earnings from London-based Shell and BP—come as Trump highlights the big profits for U.S. oil companies on the campaign trail. "I could just see the fake headlines. 'President Trump is talking about all the money they're making while people are suffering at the pump.' That'll be the headline," Trump said. "But I said, 'I don't give a damn. I'm going to say it.' We're making a freaking fortune."

In fairness, the Big Oil companies have been careful not to brag about how much they're profiting from the Iran war. After all, they don't control the global markets for oil and fuel prices, and like most corporations, they're maximizing their profits in a favorable commodities environment.

Exxon's stock is up 62% in 12 months, including a 1% hike Friday. Chevron is up 53% in a year, also counting a gain of over 1% Friday.

But the companies that focus more exclusively on oil refining have proved even bigger winners, especially from roughly 10% of global refining capacity offline in the Middle East and Russia. Phillips 66 and Valero Energy reported their most profitable quarters ever this week—$5.6 billion and $6.8 billion, respectively. Phillips 66's market cap is up 104% in a year, and Valero has risen by a whopping 140%.

articles.title: Hackers just stole $6 billion in crypto. It’s not the first time, and it won’t be the last
articles.summary: For years, the crypto industry has tried to shed its affiliation with crime while marketing itself as a safe alternative to traditional banking and investing. But once again, a record-shattering heist is deepening concerns about crypto’s vulnerabilities.
articles.body: For years, the crypto industry has tried to shed its affiliation with crime while marketing itself as a safe alternative to traditional banking and investing. But once again, a record-shattering heist is deepening concerns about crypto’s vulnerabilities. On Thursday, the world’s biggest crypto exchange, Binance, saw more than $6 billion siphoned from its system in the span of about 20 minutes. About half of those funds were linked to a kind of cryptocurrency known as stablecoins, which were quickly frozen by the firms that issue them. The other funds were tied up in digital tokens such as bitcoin and ether, which don’t have centralized governing authorities and are likely impossible to recover, according to crypto researchers. Binance’s losses could top $3 billion, according to researchers. While that is a small fraction of the exchange’s $155 billion in total user assets, it eclipses the $1 billion emergency fund Binance had set aside for situations like this. The company pledged to cover the losses with those emergency reserves and other assets, emphasizing that “user funds are safe.” Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals Thursday, just hours after a smaller security breach throttled operations at Polymarket, the crypto-powered prediction market. This was the second apparent hack of Polymarket since June and was likely unrelated to the Binance incident. Some 700 Polymarket users lost $2.7 million in unauthorized withdrawals, according to analytics firm Bubblemaps. Like Binance, Polymarket promised to make customers whole. But security experts warn that covering customer losses isn’t much of a long-term strategy. Why crypto is risky “The fact that Binance may have the balance sheet to absorb the damage is encouraging, but I wouldn’t confuse financial strength with operational security,” Ryan Kirkley, CEO of crypto infrastructure firm Global Settlement Network, said in an email. “We’re talking about the world’s largest crypto exchange relying on emergency freezes and reimbursement promises,” he said. “That’s a serious problem for an industry asking institutions to trust it with substantially more capital.” To be sure, any business can be vulnerable to a cyberattack. But centralized exchanges like Binance have become high-value targets for hackers, in part because they exist outside the strict regulations that banks and other financial institutions must adhere to. And crypto has long been favored by criminal enterprises because it can move funds quickly and anonymously across borders. Binance, which was founded in China but lacks a fixed headquarters, pleaded guilty in 2023 to violating US federal anti-money-laundering rules, among other charges — a case that landed its Canadian founder, Changpeng Zhao, in prison for four months. Zhao was pardoned by President Donald Trump last year but remains legally prohibited from running Binance. AI is turbocharging security risks across the internet. In Thursday’s Binance hack, researchers at Chainalysis said they observed “laundering patterns we have not seen before” and that “thousands of transactions in a short period suggest that the attackers are using automation to obscure the trail of funds.” How to protect yourself And despite a warm embrace from the Trump administration, crypto remains a risky business with few regulations on the books. In the United States, the vast majority of people investing in crypto do so through centralized exchanges that lack the kind of federal deposit insurance provided by traditional banks. “Centralized exchanges pose a risk because they’re centralized… once that system gets hacked, everybody’s funds can be compromised,” said Iman Shafiei, founder of Keystone Research Group, in an email. The simplest protection, he said, is to not leave funds sitting on the same exchanges where you buy and sell. “The moment you want to hold, move your crypto to a self-custody wallet.” Of course, self-custody, in which a person manages their own digital wallet, comes with its own potential headaches. If an account holder loses their password, there is no customer service hotline to call and those funds are effectively gone. In 2021, Chainalysis estimated that around 20% of all the bitcoin ever created may be lost or stranded in wallets that account holders can no longer access.

articles.title: The real question we should all be asking about AI
articles.summary: The stock market is turning its back on Big Tech.
articles.body: The stock market is turning its back on Big Tech. Google just had its worst day ever. Intel tumbled more than any day since the Nixon administration. Amazon and Meta both had significant declines this week, too. The Nasdaq tumbled and is just over a percentage point away from a correction (a 10% decline from its all-time high). The common thread: Building the infrastructure to power AI is really, really expensive – and Big Tech profits aren’t yet justifying that massive expense. AI companies are increasingly doling out more cash for data centers than their businesses are able to generate. But if the stock market is supposed be to delivering some kind of message, Big Tech isn’t hearing it. Spending on AI has reached $1.6 trillion since 2023 and is expected to hit $1 trillion every single year for the next decade or so, according to JPMorgan. None of that changed this week. That’s because the market that’s financing all of this – the bond market – is mostly shrugging its shoulders while the stock market is in the midst of a mild freakout. Lenders have been lining up to take on Big Tech’s debt to pay for the technology that’s reshaping the global economy. That means the questions the market seems to be asking about AI – will Big Tech keep growing its spending? (it most certainly will) and will AI will turn a profit anytime soon? (doesn’t look like it) – are the wrong ones. The real question we should be asking about AI is: How much longer will the bond market sustain the nonstop spending spree? That will ultimately dictate whether AI turns into a success or a bust. AI math The way AI math works is like this: Spend a lot of money upfront on the infrastructure needed to support AI (data centers, servers, chips, power, labor, building materials, etc.). Then, once the data center is switched on, AI companies can monetize that investment … somewhere between three months to two years later, according to Goldman Sachs. With profit arriving that far down the road, hyperscalers (the Big Tech guys like Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta) need to borrow a ton of money upfront and pay back investors down the road. “A ton” doesn’t really do it justice. Those four hyperscalers alone have been collectively responsible for more than a third of all capital expenditures from the S&P 500 over the past 12 months, notes John Higgins, chief economic adviser at Capital Economics. That’s why a third of Big Tech’s capital expenditures this year are expected to be financed with debt – something like $250 billion worth of bonds from hyperscalers alone, according to Goldman Sachs. That’s expected to peak next year at around 35% of hyperscalers’ spending. But bond market investors don’t have infinite money to spend. And there’s a ton of competition for lending right now – especially from US Treasuries as the government is trying to pay for Social Security, Medicare and an expensive war, all at the same time. That raises an obvious question: Exactly how much money are investors willing to lend AI companies? It’s more than you might think. The hypothetical maximum amount of debt the market can absorb is unknowable, but Goldman Sachs did the math anyway and came up with $510 billion of available investment-grade (top-tier) debt for the biggest hyperscalers. That’s more than double what they’re currently expected to be borrowing by the end of the year. In other words: The biggest AI companies have a lot of runway left to borrow. Who’s lending to whom? The question isn’t how much; the question is how much longer. The answer depends on two parts: Who is paying and who is receiving. “We are not concerned about access to capital,” said Amanda Lynam, chief credit strategist for Goldman Sachs on a recent company podcast. “We are just expecting there to be a more nuanced conversation about where to issue and at what price.” Private investment funds, venture funds and private equity are ready to do the heavy lifting to support the AI buildout, Lynam said, with trillions more dollars of “dry powder” to finance it. But hyperscalers aren’t the only game in town. Other companies, including neoclouds, are playing in the space too. They’re highly indebted companies that rent out computing to other businesses, and their credit situation is starting to look iffy. Their non-investment-grade bonds deliver high yields that investors willing to take on more risk are willing to gamble on, in exchange for potentially massive rewards.. That’s the market in which CoreWeave plays, with its bond yields surging to 15% this month as losses piled up. Elon Musk said the neocloud industry, which includes CoreWeave, is due for a massive shakeout (he called it “guppy-level death.”) Every new technology has winners and losers, and Musk may be right about neoclouds. We’ll see. Hyperscalers, by contrast, look like winners. Their cloud revenue (a stat Wall Street uses to measure AI demand) grew 50% in the second quarter. They have huge contract backlogs and the capacity to absorb higher borrowing costs. Those bottlenecks can support high prices, which helped hyperscaler revenue surge 19% over the past 12 months, according to Higgins. And the advent of agentic AI has sent demand exploding: requests from agents consume 15 times as many tokens as human-initiated requests, according to OpenRouter. “The outlook for these things doesn’t look obviously bleak, given that AI is gradually being used more and more in the economy,” Higgins said. So what’s the problem? The concern is that the cost of borrowing could get unwieldy. And that could change the economics that are still working for AI. Negative sentiment that’s pervasive in the stock market could start to bleed out into the bond market, sending bond yields higher and raising borrowing costs for AI companies. The bond market works best when there’s an end in sight, Lyman noted. Every AI investor believes there’s a light at the end of the tunnel. We just have no idea how long this tunnel is. The uncertainty about when companies will ultimately start turning a profit and making money off all their massive AI investments could give the bond market pause, she said. In the meantime, the outlook for the technology and the big companies’ finances looks quite strong, said Stephanie Aliaga, a global market strategist with JPMorgan, in a recent note to investors. Warning signs would include a downshift in businesses’ AI usage, cheaper pricing or fewer customer commitments. We’re not seeing any of those yet.

articles.title: Apple Overtakes Nvidia to Become World’s Most Valuable Company
articles.summary: Apple Inc. reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company on Friday, taking the mantle from Nvidia Corp. as investors seek the perceived safety of the...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Apple Inc. reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company on Friday, taking the mantle from Nvidia Corp. as investors seek the perceived safety of the iPhone maker amid concerns about artificial intelligence spending.

Shares of Apple fell 1.2% on Friday, resulting in a market capitalization of $5.03 trillion, while Nvidia sank 4.2% to close with a valuation of $4.93 trillion. This is the first time Apple has overtaken Nvidia since briefly doing so in late July.

Friday's selloff came as a number of major technology companies disappointed with their results, including Intel Corp. and Amazon.com Inc., which followed similarly disappointing reports from Alphabet Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc., among others. The reports renewed concerns about the outlook for AI spending, something Apple has largely foregone.

Fears that heavy spending on AI computing infrastructure won't pay off have helped make Apple, which has kept a lid on capital expenditures, by far the best performing of the Magnificent Seven tech giants this year. Its shares are up 27% in 2026, more than twice the gain of second place Nvidia, which is a key beneficiary of AI spending.

The outlays have gotten so large that companies like Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. have seen their free cash flow turn negative, forcing them to increasingly turn to debt markets for funding. Meanwhile, rising interest rates are raising the cost of borrowing.

Apple, by contrast, is projected to see its free cash flow climb 38% to $142 billion in fiscal 2026, which ended on Sept. 30.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index fell 6.7% in October, its worst month since March 2025. CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group, data center owners that offer AI computing services, have dropped more than 30% this month. With Friday's collapse, Intel lost more than 45% in October, its biggest ever one-month drop in data compiled by Bloomberg going back more than 40 years.

articles.title: Friday's rout shaved over $11 billion off the US government's stake in Intel
articles.summary: The 25%-plus drop in Intel's stock price on Friday has shaved about $10 billion from the US government's stake in the company, though the transaction remains...
articles.body:
The share price of Intel dropped almost 30% on Friday , shaving over $11 billion from the US government's stake in the company, though the transaction remains profitable overall.

Last August, the Trump administration took a 9.9% equity stake in the chipmaker at a price of $20.47 per share, according to a company press release at the time.

That initial stake of 433.3 million primary shares was worth about $8.9 billion. The value shot up dramatically earlier this year, with Intel ( INTC ) closing on Thursday at $92.07 per share, implying a value to the US government of $39.9 billion.

But the stock took a beating on Friday after the company reported earnings on Thursday night . The stock closed Friday down about 29% at $65.76 per share, suggesting a new paper value for the government's stake of $28.5 billion.

The rapid price change underscores how government investments can take investors on a wild ride and presents a new challenge to a centerpiece of Trump's government portfolio, which now spans 40 companies, according to a CATO Institute tracker.

A nearly $150 billion loss for the company

Investors punished Intel after its Q4 revenue outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations and the company reported a worse-than-anticipated drop in PC revenue.

Intel is projecting fourth quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below the $17 billion analysts expected. The company is projecting earnings per share of $0.25 versus forecasts of $0.43.

That change in outlook led to losses that, at some points on Friday morning, put Intel on pace for its worst losses since 1974 , as the company as a whole erased nearly $150 billion in market value.

The government's investment in Intel — which Trump has promised will yield outsized returns for taxpayers — is a running theme from the White House. In September, an image on Truth Social depicted the president as a stock trader in the Oval Office, with Intel's price displayed on a screen at $95 per share.

Trump has previously exaggerated the gains, suggesting at one point, "I've made Hundreds of Billions of Dollars on Stocks, and many other type Holdings, for the U.S.A., not myself."

Even so, the investment in Intel remains very profitable and still ended the day on Friday more than three times what the US paid for it.

Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
articles.summary: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.
articles.body:
Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI).

Shares in Intel plummeted by 28% on Friday, while Google owner Alphabet saw its stock price continue to fall another 1.4% after a 12% plunge on Thursday.

Other tech stocks, including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025.

While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble.

Major tech companies have ramped up artificial intelligence spending, with Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft committing to spending $800bn between them in 2026.

Alphabet's stock market value fell sharply on Thursday, taking more than $500bn (£374bn) off its market value after it revealed the AI summaries it now provides as the top answer to search queries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.

At the same time, Alphabet expects to spend up to $205bn this year on investments, almost entirely related to AI.

The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere however, with Intel shedding more than $130bn in value.

The chip maker said it planned to increase spending on AI despite weaker demand for computers, a major source of demand for its micro-processors.

On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.

"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.

In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.

Amazon on Thursday revealed it had also spent more cash than it was making, and that spending had increased six-fold over the span of three months.

The company has committed to spending $220bn this year, putting the money towards investments such as AI data centres, network equipment, and servers.

Amazon shares recovered some overnight losses, but were still down by 1.4% at the end of Friday trading.

Reddit stock plunged by 29%, after the social media platform revealed weaker-than-expected daily user figures and warned that Google's growing AI-driven search was hurting referral traffic.

articles.title: Hedge Funds Boost Natural Gas Short Positions to Most on Record
articles.summary: Hedge funds this week amassed the largest-ever short position on US natural gas on expectations that an unusually warm winter will slash demand for the furna...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Hedge funds this week amassed the largest-ever short position on US natural gas on expectations that an unusually warm winter will slash demand for the furnace and power-plant fuel.

Money managers boosted their short-only exposure, or bets on prices falling, across seven benchmark Henry Hub contracts to 625,150, according to Commodity Futures Trading Commission data released Friday. That's the largest in data going back to May 2013, breaking the most recent short-only record which was set just a week earlier.

The net-short position on US gas rose to 223,591, the most bearish overall position since February 2020, when the outbreak of Covid-19 crushed demand for fuels and throttled markets across asset classes. The all-time largest net-short position, set in February 2020, was 266,416.

Benchmark US gas futures for delivery in December, which is currently the front-month, plummeted 18% to $2.898 per million British thermal units over the past three weeks as weather forecasts continued to shift warmer. Above-normal temperatures are now expected across the northern US for the first two weeks of November, according to the private forecaster Commodity Weather Group. The north is where most US heating demand is concentrated.

The bearish bets reflect traders' growing conviction that the so-called Super El Niño weather pattern will bring very mild weather. They also increase the risk of a short squeeze. Any sudden, severe cold snap can send gas demand surging while slashing production, lifting prices as traders scramble to rapidly close out short positions to forestall losses.

articles.title: Starbucks wants to trial a 'fast pass' drive-through with AI
articles.summary: With roughly half of Starbucks consumers using the drive-through, the company said it plans to test background AI models to speed up service.
articles.body:
Starbucks wants baristas to recognize you, your order, and your car as soon as you enter the drive-through lane with artificial intelligence and its app.

With roughly half of Starbucks consumers using the drive-through, the company said it plans to test background AI models to help baristas enter orders faster and more accurately.

"We're going to have, almost, the ability to have a fast pass for the drive-through," CEO Brian Niccol told Yahoo Finance following its latest quarterly results. He said that when customers pull through the drive-through with the app open, it will show their recent orders, so baristas can ask, "The usual?"

Once customers confirm, "It's paid," Niccol added. "Now you're off to the window to pick up your drink, and out you go. It'll be the fastest drive-through experience you can have."

To order ahead, pay with the app, and earn reward stars, customers are required to create a Starbucks account and sign in. Niccol's "fast pass" comment drew comparisons to Disney's "fast pass" on X, but unlike Disney's fast pass, the Starbucks app is free.

This past quarter, the Starbucks loyalty program's 90-day active members reached a record 36 million. Those customers tend to drive transactions and sales growth, which rose 7.2% in the fourth quarter.

These investments by Starbucks come as the coffee chain faces growing competition from drive-through-focused chains like Dutch Bros ( BROS ), 7Brew, and Scooter's Coffee. Plus, more customers are coming for afternoon pick-me-ups and small treats in their order.

TD Cowen analyst Andrew Charles thinks the afternoon is a prime opportunity.

"We expect a greater focus on the afternoon daypart, via beverage innovation and marketing support, where drive-thru competitors have found success," he wrote in a note to clients. "We interpret a greater focus on caffeine-free refreshers to help drive engagement with kids."

articles.title: Alphabet’s October wipeout hits $758 billion, its worst month ever
articles.summary: Alphabet lost $468 billion in market value this week, more than SpaceX, Intel and Nvidia combined, capping its worst month ever.
articles.body:
Big Tech's brutal week had one clear epicenter. Alphabet ( GOOGL ) lost $468 billion in market value this week, more than SpaceX, Intel and Nvidia combined.

That was the Google parent's worst week ever and the second-biggest weekly wipeout for any US-listed stock, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Only Nvidia ( NVDA ) has lost more, about $552 billion in the week of Jan. 27, 2025, when China's DeepSeek rattled AI investors. Alphabet's previous worst was about $386 billion in the week ended June 26.

Most of the damage came Thursday, when Alphabet lost $475 billion in a single session after its third quarter results . Friday's slide wiped out the gains the stock had made earlier in the week.

October was even worse. Alphabet shed about $758 billion in market value this month, the second-biggest monthly loss ever for a US-listed company. Only SpaceX ( SPCX ) has lost more, about $822 billion in July. Alphabet's October loss is nearly double its previous worst month, about $420 billion in February 2025.

In percentage terms, the stock fell nearly 19% in October, its worst month since it went public in 2004. Its previous worst was an 18.5% drop in November 2008. For the week, it fell nearly 13%, its worst since August 2011.

SpaceX, Intel ( INTC ) and Nvidia each lost more than $100 billion in market value this week. Intel fell as much as 30% Friday after a weak outlook, its steepest drop in decades . Amazon ( AMZN ) shed about $80 billion for the week after reporting results Thursday. Some software names fell harder in percentage terms, with ServiceNow ( NOW ) and Fortinet ( FTNT ) down roughly 25% to 34%.

Not all of that money left the market. Eli Lilly ( LLY ), Tesla ( TSLA ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) added more than $300 billion in combined value, even as the Magnificent 7 stumbled .

UBS's chief investment office argued against heading for the exits. "Further volatility does not make retreating from markets an effective way to protect portfolios from potential drawdowns, in our view," Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, CIO Americas and global head of equities, wrote Friday. "We continue to see scope for equity gains overall and believe investors should focus on building a resilient portfolio that includes exposure beyond tech."

The close settled it. October goes down as Alphabet's worst month since its IPO, in dollars and in percentage terms. The stock finished the week about $7 above the roughly $273 level it would have needed to take Nvidia's weekly record.

articles.title: NHAI’s free-flow tolling push to cut land acquisition needs, cap toll plaza lanes at 8
articles.summary: New Delhi: All future national highway projects, including those where construction is yet to begin, will have toll plazas with not more than eight lanes,
articles.body: New Delhi: All future national highway projects, including those where construction is yet to begin, will have toll plazas with not more than eight lanes, as NHAI has made Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling an integral part of highway development. The move will reduce land acquisition requirements and save public money, as electronic toll collection equipment will be mounted on overhead gantries instead of requiring multiple tolling lanes and booths.At present, several toll plazas on six- and eight-lane highways, particularly around major cities, have over 20 lanes and in some cases this goes up to 32 lanes. In conventional tolling systems, more tolling lanes were required to clear vehicles queuing up at toll gates.“For all practical reasons, there will be no need to acquire any extra land for toll plazas. The tolling system using gantry-mounted high-performance RFID readers and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras to identify vehicles in motion and deduct the applicable toll through FASTag will be installed on the highway,” said an official.The revised design seeks to rationalise the number of tolling lanes by increasing the vehicle-handling capacity of each lane. NHAI has estimated the throughput of each lane at 600 vehicles per hour while prescribing the new configuration. An additional over-dimension or spare lane will also be provided to handle emergencies.The circular also lays down safety and infrastructure requirements, including a minimum six-metre clearance for gantry-mounted equipment, advance signage, variable message signs around one-km before the plaza and adequate high-mast lighting. Toll plazas will, wherever feasible, be located on straight stretches of highways.The policy will apply to highway projects at different stages of construction. Projects still under the detailed project report (DPR) stage will incorporate the new layout in their bidding documents. For projects already awarded or under construction where toll plaza construction has not started, the revised design will be adopted through changes in the scope of work.NHAI has directed all regional officers, project implementation units and DPR consultants to incorporate the new provisions in upcoming projects and ensure their adoption in ongoing projects wherever applicable. The revised policy supersedes the earlier toll plaza design guidelines for four-lane and wider highways, while two-lane highways with paved shoulders will continue under the existing tolling system.You use AI every day. articles.body: MUMBAI: Reliance Industries, India's most valuable company by market capitalisation, reported a 34% rise in second-quarter profit for FY27 to Rs 29,550 crore on Friday, beating analysts' average estimate of Rs 21,419 crore. Stronger transportation fuel and downstream margins drove the gain.Jio Platforms, which made a blockbuster stock market debut this week, posted an 18% rise in ebitda to Rs 22,223 crore on strong revenue growth, operating leverage and a 250-basis-point margin expansion. RIL said performance was affected by the shift in the festive calendar to the third quarter.Ebitda at the oil and gas division slipped 2% to Rs 4,901 crore due to lower revenue and higher govt levies. articles.title: Power, fertiliser fuel LNG import surge
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's LNG imports rose 17.4% to a record 2.7 million tonnes so far in Oct on the back of higher demand from the power, fertiliser and city
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's LNG imports rose 17.4% to a record 2.7 million tonnes so far in Oct on the back of higher demand from the power, fertiliser and city gas distribution sectors. Besides, more cargo arrived from Qatar and the UAE, data from maritime intelligence and research firm Kpler showed.Crude imports also reached a record 5.6 million barrels per day (mbd) during the month, 14% higher than a year ago, with Russia remaining the top supplier, while shipments from West Asia and the Atlantic Basin also rose.LNG supplies increased as India's domestic production has declined, pushing up the import dependence from 50% to nearly 52%. In addition, companies are seen to be stocking up the gas for the power sector, as solar energy is set to decline in winters, and the fertiliser sector will need higher feedstock for production.According to Kpler data, the record LNG imports in Oct can be attributed to a sharp rebound in supplies from Qatar, which had remained curtailed due to disruptions in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz during the West Asia conflict. Qatar has traditionally been the biggest supplier of LNG to India, accounting for 40-50% of total imported volumes. In Sept last year, India imported nearly 2.1 MT of LNG, of which 0.8 MT came from Qatar. India received more than 0.4 MT of LNG from Qatar this month, the highest volume since the war broke out. The supplies were 370% more than the 0.1 MT received from the West Asian nation in Sept, and only marginally lower than the cumulative imports between March and Sept.Despite its production facilities being impacted, sources said Qatar was willing to increase LNG supplies and meet its long-term commitments to customers.The US, however, continued to remain the biggest supplier of LNG, with 0.6 MT of supplies till Oct 29. The UAE, Oman, Angola, Nigeria and Australia were other major suppliers during the month. Though Russian crude flows have declined from a peak of 2.8 mbd in July to nearly 2 mbd in Oct, Moscow remained the largest supplier, accounting for nearly 36% of total imports.Nikhil Dubey, Kpler's lead analyst - refining, however, said elevated freight costs of Russian barrels had eroded their delivered-price advantage, while improved supplies from West Asia offered competitive alternatives to refiners. articles.body: More than $2 trillion in market value is set to be wiped from the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 this month, as Big Tech earnings intensified investor scrutiny of whether the billions being poured into artificial intelligence can generate returns quickly enough.The wipeout would amount to slightly more than SpaceX's entire market value. The index has fallen over 5.8% so far in Oct as the AI trade ran into turbulence, with hyperscalers Meta Platforms, Alphabet and Amazon.com raising spending forecasts further as they race to expand AI infrastructure.The prospect of ever-bigger AI outlays has unnerved investors, particularly as rising borrowing costs threaten to make debt-funded investment more expensive and harder to justify.Alphabet suffered its biggest one-day percentage drop on record on Thursday after disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn. Meta's plans for a record $97.5 billion fund raise heightened concerns about shareholder dilution and whether mounting AI spending could force other Big Tech companies to increasingly tap capital markets.On Friday, Intel's stock led the way lower and was flirting with its worst day since 1974 after tumbling 30%.Microsoft and SpaceX broke from the gloom, with results that showed AI spending starting to pay off."It may be that we've overestimated how strong the growth might be, but they're not going negative in aggregate," said John Bilton, global head of strategic research at Multi-Asset Solutions."We have an insatiable and growing demand for data." Microsoft is reportedly planning to raise about $25 billion through its first US investment-grade bond sale in more than nine years. Among other hyperscalers, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet have issued hundreds of billions of dollars in bond sales over the past four years, worrying investors about overreliance on the medium for raising capital. Morgan Stanley forecast capital spending on AI infrastructure overall will surpass a trillion dollars next year. AI companies' growing reliance on debt funding is emerging as a new risk for investors, challenging the view that the companies at the heart of the boom are insulated from macroeconomic pressures.The concern is spreading beyond stocks to credit markets, where investors are starting to price in the possibility that rising financing costs, combined with slower returns on AI spending, could squeeze companies previously viewed as relatively insulated. Revenue across the "Magnificent Seven" has remained strong since ChatGPT's launch in 2022, showcasing insatiable demand and perhaps why investors were initially willing to back the spending, even as the timeline of payoffs remains uncertain.Amazon's cloud computing cash cow, Amazon Web Services, continued to accelerate, while Meta offered better-than-expected revenue growth and an upbeat outlook. Microsoft also forecast strong cloud growth in its latest earnings report.Big Tech has historically spent heavily on infrastructure to build and expand businesses such as cloud computing, online advertising and e-commerce, but the AI boom has pushed capital expenditure to dizzying levels. articles.title: IA virou um problema para as gigantes de tecnologia? Entenda o tombo bilionário nas bolsas | G1
articles.standfirst: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta e Microsoft perderam quase US$ 900 bilhões em valor de mercado após balanços. Investidores questionam se os aportes bilionários em inteligência artificial vão se transformar em receita e lucro.
articles.summary: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta e Microsoft perderam quase US$ 900 bilhões em valor de mercado após balanços. Investidores questionam se os aportes bilionários em inteligência artificial vão se transformar em receita e lucro.
articles.body:
As gigantes de tecnologia estão gastando cada vez mais dinheiro para avançar na corrida pela inteligência artificial (IA) . Mas, em vez de empolgar, os investimentos bilionários começaram a acender um alerta na bolsa: o mercado quer saber quando essas empresas vão conseguir transformar tanto dinheiro gasto em lucro .

Na quinta-feira (29), após a divulgação dos resultados trimestrais, as ações da Alphabet, dona do Google, despencaram 12,64%, na maior queda diária da empresa desde sua abertura de capital , em 2004. Os balanços trouxeram números elevados de investimentos em infraestrutura de IA e projeções de novos gastos bilionários, aumentando a preocupação dos investidores com o ritmo de expansão das empresas.

Segundo levantamento da consultoria Elos Ayta, a desvalorização fez a companhia perder US$ 493,9 bilhões em valor de mercado em um único pregão. Para se ter uma ideia, o montante equivale a 55,82% de todo o valor de mercado das empresas listadas na bolsa brasileira, estimado em US$ 885 bilhões.

A queda ajudou a pressionar Wall Street e fez parte de um movimento mais amplo de desvalorização entre empresas do setor.

📲 Após o fechamento, a Amazon também sofreu uma forte queda , de aproximadamente 7%, que retirou quase US$ 200 bilhões de seu valor de mercado. Juntas, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta e Microsoft perderam quase US$ 900 bilhões em valor de mercado após a divulgação dos resultados do terceiro trimestre.

A pressão se intensificou ao longo do pregão desta sexta-feira (30). No fechamento, o Nasdaq recuou 2,9%, aos 25.437 pontos, depois de atingir o menor nível em quase três meses. O S&P 500 caiu 1,8%, aos 7.580 pontos, enquanto o Dow Jones perdeu 1,1%, aos 51.770 pontos.

A pressão também atingiu as gigantes de tecnologia e as fabricantes de chips. No fechamento, a Amazon recuou 1,49%, enquanto a Alphabet também terminou em queda, após despencar 12,64% na véspera.

A Intel teve um dos piores desempenhos do pregão: suas ações desabaram 28,6%, na maior queda diária desde 1974. A desvalorização, porém, também reflete problemas próprios da companhia. A fabricante alertou que deve consumir caixa neste ano, diante da fraqueza do mercado de computadores pessoais, de dificuldades na fabricação de chips e dos altos investimentos para ampliar sua capacidade de produção.

O movimento também atingiu outras empresas do setor. A Nvidia caiu 4,2%, a AMD perdeu 10,9% e o índice de semicondutores recuou 7,2%.

➡️ Em outubro, o Nasdaq 100 acumulava queda superior a 5,8%. A desvalorização poderia eliminar mais de US$ 2 trilhões em valor de mercado do índice no mês.

Tombo das ações reduz em US$ 70 bilhões fortuna de três bilionários

A desvalorização das gigantes de tecnologia também atingiu o patrimônio de alguns dos homens mais ricos do mundo.

Como boa parte da fortuna desses empresários está ligada às participações que mantêm nas empresas que fundaram, a queda das ações na bolsa reduz o valor estimado de seus bens.

Segundo o Bloomberg Billionaires Index, Larry Page e Sergey Brin, cofundadores do Google, tiveram uma redução conjunta de US$ 60,7 bilhões em suas fortunas na quinta-feira (29). Page perdeu aproximadamente US$ 31,6 bilhões, enquanto a fortuna de Brin encolheu US$ 29,1 bilhões.

Jeff Bezos, fundador da Amazon, também foi afetado . O empresário registrou uma redução estimada de US$ 9,48 bilhões em seu patrimônio no mesmo dia. Somadas, as perdas dos três bilionários chegaram a US$ 70,18 bilhões.

A redução não significa que os empresários tenham retirado esse dinheiro de suas contas bancárias ou vendido ações com prejuízo. Trata-se de uma queda no valor estimado de suas fortunas, influenciada principalmente pela desvalorização das participações que possuem nas companhias.

Investimentos em IA disparam, mas mercado cobra resultados

Por trás da pressão sobre as ações está o tamanho dos investimentos que as empresas estão fazendo para desenvolver e ampliar seus negócios de inteligência artificial (IA).

Segundo a Reuters, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft e Alphabet elevaram juntas os investimentos em infraestrutura de US$ 113 bilhões para US$ 207 bilhões em um ano. A previsão é de outros US$ 232 bilhões em investimentos no trimestre seguinte.

Para 2026, os gastos de capital dessas quatro empresas podem chegar a US$ 740 bilhões, segundo estimativas citadas pela agência. Os recursos são destinados principalmente à construção de centros de processamento de dados, compra de chips e expansão da infraestrutura necessária para treinar e operar sistemas de inteligência artificial.

A Amazon, por exemplo, investiu cerca de US$ 75,9 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, acima dos US$ 58,7 bilhões esperados pelo mercado. A Alphabet destinou mais de US$ 50 bilhões à expansão de sua infraestrutura. A Microsoft investiu US$ 45,2 bilhões, enquanto a Meta registrou gastos de US$ 35 bilhões no período.

Em outro levantamento, também divulgado pela Reuters, os números mostram o peso desses investimentos sobre o caixa das companhias. Dessa vez, a análise considera cinco empresas: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta e Oracle.

Nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, as cinco empresas investiram juntas US$ 556,9 bilhões, valor superior aos US$ 542,9 bilhões que geraram com suas operações no mesmo período. Com isso, o grupo passou de um saldo positivo de US$ 143,5 bilhões em fluxo de caixa livre nos primeiros nove meses de 2025 para um resultado negativo de US$ 14 bilhões neste ano.

O fluxo de caixa livre é o dinheiro que sobra depois que a empresa paga suas despesas operacionais e investimentos. Quando esse indicador fica negativo, significa que os recursos gerados pelas operações não foram suficientes para cobrir os gastos do período.

Analistas apontam que a questão é que esses investimentos levam tempo para gerar retorno. Enquanto as empresas gastam bilhões para ampliar sua capacidade, os investidores querem entender quando esse dinheiro vai se transformar em novas receitas e, principalmente, em lucro.

"O mercado continua confiante na demanda por inteligência artificial, como mostram os resultados crescentes da área de computação em nuvem. Mas os investidores passaram a cobrar mais das empresas: não basta anunciar grandes investimentos em IA, é preciso mostrar que eles estão se transformando em receita e, principalmente, em geração de caixa", afirma Nickolas Lobo, especialista de investimentos da Nomad.

Ou seja, não basta mostrar que a empresa está construindo centros de dados e comprando chips. Os investidores querem ver se a estrutura vai gerar dinheiro suficiente para compensar o que foi gasto.

"São bilhões de dólares destinados a centros de dados, chips e infraestrutura, enquanto a capacidade de transformar tudo isso em receita ainda está sendo construída", diz Celso Camilo, doutor em inteligência artificial e professor da Universidade Federal de Goiás (UFG).

Até agora, parte importante dos investimentos vinha do próprio dinheiro gerado pelos negócios. Com os gastos cada vez maiores, porém, as empresas também têm recorrido à emissão de dívidas e de ações para levantar recursos.

A Microsoft, por exemplo, levantou US$ 25 bilhões em uma emissão de títulos de dívida. Segundo a empresa, os recursos poderão ser utilizados para diferentes finalidades corporativas, incluindo investimentos de capital.

O movimento ocorre em um momento em que os investidores também acompanham a possibilidade de juros mais altos nos próximos anos. Com juros maiores, os empréstimos ficam mais caros e podem aumentar o custo dos projetos.

"A escala de gastos não tem precedentes. O ciclo começou com recursos próprios, avançou para a emissão de dívidas e agora chega à captação de recursos no mercado de ações", afirma.

Ele se refere também à possibilidade de as empresas emitirem novas ações para captar dinheiro. Nesse caso, os acionistas existentes podem ter sua participação proporcional reduzida, caso não acompanhem a operação.

A queda das ações reacendeu a discussão sobre uma possível bolha em torno da inteligência artificial. Isso não significa, porém, que os especialistas considerem a tecnologia uma promessa sem fundamento.

"A tecnologia é real, já está sendo utilizada e tem capacidade de transformar diversos setores da economia. O que considero exagerado são algumas expectativas de valorização", afirma Celso Camilo.

Para ele, o risco está na diferença entre o potencial da tecnologia e o preço que os investidores aceitam pagar hoje pelas ações, considerando lucros que ainda não chegaram.

Lobo também pondera que a discussão não deve ser resumida à ideia de que a IA é uma bolha. Na avaliação dele, o mercado está mais atento ao ritmo de crescimento dos investimentos e à capacidade de as empresas transformarem esse dinheiro em resultados.

"O vencedor da próxima etapa não será necessariamente quem investe mais, mas quem gera retorno sobre o capital investido", afirma.

articles.title: Reforma tributária: novo imposto sobre consumo pode ficar acima de 30% e superar o de países ricos; veja a comparação | G1
articles.standfirst: Depois da divulgação de proposta do TCU, em patamar acima do esperado, analistas passaram a apontar que o imposto brasileiro será de ao menos 30% em 2033.
articles.summary: Depois da divulgação de proposta do TCU, em patamar acima do esperado, analistas passaram a apontar que o imposto brasileiro será de ao menos 30% em 2033.
articles.body:
O cálculo foi feito por técnicos do tribunal com base em dados da Receita Federal . O percentual será encaminhado ao Congresso Nacional, que poderá concordar ou não .

Caberá ao Senado, até 15 de dezembro , fixar o valor final da alíquota, que será cobrada a partir de 2027.

▶️Para mensurar o valor da CBS, técnicos do tribunal estimaram quanto seria arrecadado com os impostos que estão sendo extintos no fim de 2026 (PIS, Cofins e grande parte do IPI). Isso porque, uma das premissas da reforma sobre o consumo, é manter o atual patamar da carga tributária.

🔎 Em 2024, o governo estimou que a alíquota da CBS seria de 8,8% . Cálculo da consultoria Roit apontava para uma alíquota de 9,43% em 2027. Estimativas divulgadas em julho pelo Comitê Gestor do IBS, dos estados, apontam que a CBS teria uma taxa de cerca de 9,2% no próximo ano.

▶️Além da CBS do governo federal, a reforma tributária também contempla a cobrança do IBS estadual e municipal, que terá uma alíquota marginal de 0,1% até 2028. A partir de 2029, os estados e municípios começam a aumentar, gradualmente, a cobrança do IBS. A cobrança integral começa em 2033.

▶️ Antes de a alíquota da CBS ser proposta pelo TCU , estimativa do Comitê Gestor do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (CGIBS) apontava que a alíquota cheia estiver sendo cobrada do imposto sobre o consumo do governo federal, estados e municípios, somaria cerca de 28% .

▶️Depois da divulgação da proposta do tribunal para a CBS, bem acima do esperado, analistas passaram a apontar que o imposto brasileiro será de ao menos 30% em 2033 — o primeiro ano com tributação cheia. O g1 considerou o patamar de 30% para comparação internacional.

▶️ Se confirmada, seria maior do que a alíquota de todos os países desenvolvidos , segundo ranking da Tax Foundation — organização sem fins lucrativos que faz avaliações sobre impostos e coleta dados sobre tributos ao redor do mundo.

▶️De acordo com o levantamento, alíquota média dos impostos gerais sobre o consumo nos países da OCDE foi de 19,4% , bem abaixo do valor estimado para o futuro IVA brasileiro. O ranking, com dados de 2026, foi divulgado em 19 de outubro ( veja abaixo ).

Alíquotas do imposto sobre o consumo — Foto: Ranking da Tax Foundation e estimativa de analistas para o Brasil

➡️O governo federal, por sua vez, alega que, atualmente, os impostos cobrados sobre o consumo no país são ainda maiores, com tributação média de cerca de 34% – mas que há dificuldade em calcular o peso dos impostos pois o sistema é muito complexo, há exceções. Além disso, alguns tributos incidem sobre si mesmos (por dentro, em cascata).

➡️Este modelo "por dentro" torna mais difícil identificar quanto de imposto está efetivamente embutido no preço de um produto ou serviço. Por isso, as notas fiscais trazem apenas uma estimativa "do valor aproximado de tributos". Com a reforma tributária, eles passarão a ser cobrados por fora (aparecerão separados do valor do produto ou serviço).

➡️Um dos problemas que resultaram em um alto imposto sobre o consumo no Brasil foi a decisão do governo do presidente Lula, e de legisladores, de terem proposto e aprovado que o atual peso dos impostos nessa base de tributação fosse mantido .

🔎A consequência da concentração maior da carga tributária brasileira sobre o consumo no Brasil é o alto grau de "regressividade" (se arrecada proporcionalmente mais de quem ganha menos) — prejudicando, dessa forma, os mais pobres.

Ao mesmo tempo, os tributos sobre o lucro, renda e o ganho de capital do brasileiro, focados nos contribuintes mais ricos, estão bem abaixo da média da OCDE, formada por países mais desenvolvidos.

Para Luís Garcia, advogado tributarista pela USP/SP e sócio do Tax Group, o alto patamar do endividamento do setor público e a rigidez das despesas mantêm a pressão por arrecadação e impedem que a reorganização dos tributos, isoladamente, produza alívio fiscal.

“A reforma tributária pode significar simplificação, mas jamais redução de carga tributária enquanto o Brasil continuar refém de uma política fiscal irresponsável”, avaliou o tributarista Luís Garcia.

▶️Outro entrave, este relacionado ao fato de que a alíquota proposta pelo TCU ficou acima do estimado anteriormente por analistas, tem a ver com as exceções aprovadas na tramitação da reforma tributária no Congresso Nacional, ou seja, com os benefícios concedidos na aquisição de determinados produtos e serviços.

Considerando a premissa básica de que a reforma deve manter o atual nível de arrecadação dos tributos sobre o consumo, os benefícios concedidos a determinados produtos e setores resultam em uma alíquota de referência mais elevada para as atividades que não contam com incentivos fiscais, algo que já havia sido apontado, à época, por representantes da indústria nacional.

Entre os benefícios aprovados na tramitação da reforma tributária, estão alíquota zero para a cesta básica, incluindo as proteínas (o que, segundo especialistas, beneficia a população mais rica), para uma lista de medicamentos e dispositivos médicos.

O Congresso aprovou ainda alíquotas reduzidas para serviços de educação e saúde; medicamentos e dispositivos médicos; produções artísticas, culturais, jornalísticas e audiovisuais nacionais; atividades desportivas; e profissões regulamentadas e fiscalizadas por conselhos profissionais.

A Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC) manifestou preocupação com a alíquota de referência de 11,3% pois ela reforça o risco de aumento da carga tributária para as empresas. A preocupação é especialmente relevante para prestadores de serviços sujeitos atualmente à alíquota conjunta de 3,65% de PIS/Cofins no regime cumulativo.

"A substituição por uma CBS com referência de 11,3% representa uma elevação expressiva da alíquota nominal, embora o impacto efetivo dependa dos créditos e do tratamento tributário de cada atividade. Empresas intensivas em mão de obra ficam mais expostas, pois a folha de pagamentos não gera créditos", avaliou a CNC, por meio de nota.

A Associação Brasileira da Indústria de Alimentos (ABIA) informou considerar preocupante a proposta de fixação da alíquota de referência de 11,3% para a CBS, bem acima das estimativas anteriores. Avalia que uma diferença dessa magnitude "ameaça elevar a carga tributária das empresas, com efeitos que podem se refletir nos preços ao consumidor".

"A definição da alíquota não deve ignorar os impactos sobre a produção, os investimentos e o custo dos alimentos. Além de aumentar os preços, uma alíquota elevada da CBS ameaça ampliar a pressão sobre o orçamento das famílias de menor renda, comprometendo seu acesso à alimentação", acrescentou a ABIA, em nota.

Paulo Skaf, presidente da Federação das Indústrias do Estado de São Paulo (Fiesp) , disse que o patamar de 11,3% estimado pelo TCU quebra a premissa central da reforma tributária de manutenção da carga fiscal.

Segundo ele, estudos técnicos apontavam equilíbrio em torno de 9% para o imposto, e que a nova projeção retira da economia mais de R$ 100 bilhões em tributos adicionais já em 2027, empurrando o IVA Dual (CBS + IBS) para além de 30% - a maior taxa do mundo.

"A produção, os investimentos e o emprego não suportam mais impostos. O reequilíbrio fiscal do Brasil exige corte e controle de gastos públicos, e não aumento de arrecadação sobre quem produz. Esperamos o bom senso do Senado Federal para corrigir essa distorção", declarou o presidente da Fiesp.

A Conexis Brasil Digital , Sindicato Nacional das Empresas de Telefonia e de Serviço Móvel, Celular e Pessoal, informou ter recebido com preocupação a proposta de fixação da alíquota de referência de 11,3% para a CBS.

"A alíquota proposta é bem superior à alíquota neutra do setor de telecomunicações. Isso representará aumento da carga tributária de telecom, prejudicando investimentos em inovação e expansão da rede, com impacto no custo do serviço para o consumidor”, disse Marcos Ferrari, presidente-executivo da Conexis Brasil Digital.

articles.title: Brazil summons Argentinian diplomat over Bolsonaro’s flight to US
articles.summary: The move threatens to further strain relations between Brazilian President Lula and his Argentinian counterpart, Milei.
articles.body:
Brazil has summoned Argentina’s top diplomat in the country to answer questions about right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro , who fled first to Argentina, then to the United States, after losing Sunday’s presidential election.

On Thursday, Brazil’s Foreign Ministry called in Argentina’s charge d’affaires, Maria Emilia Cortes, sources inside the government told the news agency Reuters.

Argentina’s Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno, however, has denied on social media that his government received a formal request for explanations regarding Bolsonaro’s decision to flee into Argentina late on Tuesday.

The circumstances surrounding Bolsonaro’s departure threaten to further strain relations between Brazil’s recently re-elected President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his Argentinian counterpart, libertarian Javier Milei.

After Sunday’s election, Bolsonaro was given a deadline to surrender his passports. Officials ordered him to remain in the country as part of an ongoing legal case.

He is part of an ongoing investigation into a money-laundering scheme, known as the Banco Master scandal.

Investigators are probing a multimillion-dollar payment Bolsonaro received from Banco Master’s former head, Daniel Vorcaro, allegedly to finance a film about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.

The younger Bolsonaro has denied any wrongdoing and called the case politically motivated.

A senator since 2019, Bolsonaro ran this year as the right-wing presidential candidate for his father’s political movement, the Liberal Party.

But after advancing to the run-off, the senator fell short by more than 4 million votes. Lula won Sunday’s race with 51.8 percent of the vote, securing a historic fourth non-consecutive term.

Bolsonaro, however, has refused to concede, though the Liberal Party has acknowledged Lula’s victory.

Instead, he made an unsubstantiated allegation of electoral malfeasance, pointing to a Supreme Court decision to extend voting hours on Sunday.

Both candidates’ campaigns had requested extensions, though for different reasons: Bolsonaro’s camp pointed to inclement weather delaying voters in parts of Brazil, while Lula’s party raised concerns about efforts to restrict public transport on election day.

But Bolsonaro argued that the last-minute extension had disadvantaged voters in regions considered right-wing strongholds.

After arriving in Miami on Wednesday, he declared himself the “legitimate president-elect” of Brazil.

He, his wife and two daughters had travelled from Brazil through northern Argentina, before boarding a chartered aircraft that passed through Ecuador to reach the US.

US President Donald Trump and Milei, both right-wing leaders, have been openly supportive of the Bolsonaro family.

The Brazilian senator later thanked Milei for his assistance, although he did not provide details about the nature of the help. A spokesperson for the Argentinian president described the journey as a rescue.

Bolsonaro, the spokesperson said, had escaped “from the claws of communism, which seeks to imprison all opposition figures”.

Trump, too, has suggested that Sunday’s election was “rigged”, though he declined to “take sides” after the result was announced.

The US president has previously issued sanctions and tariffs in response to the prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro, after the former Brazilian president denied his defeat in the 2022 election. He was convicted in 2024 of plotting a coup to prevent Lula from taking power and sentenced to 27 years in prison.

Relations between Lula and Milei have been strained since the Argentinian leader took office in 2023. Milei has repeatedly criticised Lula.

The diplomatic dispute follows an earlier deterioration in relations, with the South American countries each recalling their ambassadors in August after a series of public disagreements.

articles.title: Wall Street reels from tech selloff as Nasdaq posts biggest single-day fall since June
articles.summary: US stocks ended Friday's session with significant losses, as concerns over the scale of investments in artificial intelligence (AI) and the time required
articles.body: US stocks ended Friday's session with significant losses, as concerns over the scale of investments in artificial intelligence (AI) and the time required to generate returns weighed on investor sentiment. Disappointing quarterly performances from Intel and Amazon further fuelled the technology selloff, pushing the Nasdaq composite to its steepest single-day percentage decline since June 5, according to a Reuters report.The Nasdaq plunged 2.86 per cent to settle at 25,437.00, while the S&P 500 shed 1.82 per cent to close at 7,580.07. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also slipped 1.09 per cent, ending the session at 51,770.31.The technology-focused Nasdaq has now retreated 7.8 per cent from its record closing high registered on October 6. The latest wave of selling came after intel and amazon released their quarterly results late on Thursday, prompting investors to reassess the prospects of companies making substantial investments in AI.Intel shares suffered a steep 28.6 per cent decline, while other major chipmakers also witnessed heavy selling. Nvidia dropped 4.2 per cent and AMD lost 10.9 per cent. The broader semiconductor index tumbled 7.2 per cent, taking its monthly decline beyond 15 per cent.Server manufacturers were not spared either, with Dell shares falling 10.8 per cent and HP declining 9.6 per cent."It's fair to say that this week, not just today, has been very much about the future of AI and what that's going to look like, whether there will be a positive return on investment and if so, how quickly," Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors in New York, told Reuters.Pursche noted that companies delivering results in line with or above elevated market expectations were continuing to perform well, while those missing targets were facing significant selling pressure.The weakness extended beyond individual stocks. The S&P 500's broader technology sector registered its largest monthly percentage decline since March 2025. Meanwhile, the communication services sector recorded its sharpest monthly fall since April 2022.However, the overall corporate earnings picture remained encouraging despite the market downturn. According to LSEG data cited by reuters, 82 per cent of the 299 S&P 500 companies that had announced their third-quarter results had exceeded analysts' consensus estimates. Analysts had projected year-on-year earnings growth of 31.6 per cent for the quarter.Cryptocurrency-linked stocks also came under pressure following reports that hackers had stolen USD 6.3 billion from binance. Shares of coinbase, strategy and robinhood declined between 7.2 per cent and 10.6 per cent.According to the news agency ANI, All three key US stock indices ended the week in the red, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also posting losses for the month.You use AI every day.
